persistent_identifier_status: Repository-local stable dataset identifier. Source article DOI is provided; no separate dataset DOI was identified.
title: Yield-weighted elemental composition of Kassel urban roadside grass under two- and four-cut management
citation: Piepenschneider, M., De Moor, S., Hensgen, F., Meers, E., & Wachendorf, M. (2015). Element concentrations in urban grass cuttings from roadside verges in the face of energy recovery. Environmental Science and Pollution Research, 22(10), 7808–7820. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11356-014-3881-9. Full table transcription checked against Piepenschneider, M. (2015), Urban Grass and Grass-Leaf Litter Mixtures as Source for Bioenergy Recovery, University of Kassel dissertation, Table 3.
source_locations: Dissertation Chapter 2 Table 3, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 28); plant sampling and processing, printed pp. 10–11 (PDF pp. 21–22); analytical methods, printed pp. 13–14 (PDF pp. 24–25)
geography: Ten urban roadside-verge sites in Kassel, Germany
license: No explicit open reuse license identified for the thesis or article. This dataset contains a limited attributed transcription of published table values; verify rights before external redistribution.
material_scope: Grass harvested under two-cut and four-cut regimes from urban roadside verges; Table 3 reports yield-weighted mean elemental concentrations and ash content.
experimental_conditions: Ten sites. Vegetation samples were cut at 5 cm. Plant material for elemental analysis was dried at 65 C before analysis. Ca, K, Mg, Na, P and trace elements were analyzed after acid digestion; N was measured by elemental analysis. Sulfur and silicon were measured only for two-cut material. Table 3 labels its values as yield-weighted means.
data_scope: 34 records: 17 reported analytes/properties for each management regime. Cd and Pb values are censored below reported detection limits. Four-cut sulfur and silicon are explicitly not reported, not zero.
basis_note: The methods state that dried plant material was analyzed. Table 3 does not explicitly label its reported concentration denominators as dry matter, so this dataset records the method basis and leaves the tabular DM denominator status unresolved.
limitations: German urban roadside grass is a comparator, not Dutch roadside-grass measurement or VARTA feedstock.
Only yield-weighted management means are available here. Site-level observations, weighting values and analyte-specific sample counts are not transcribed in Table 3.
Below-detection Cd and Pb are censored observations. They are not zeros or exact quantified means.
Sulfur and silicon were measured only for the two-cut regime; four-cut values are unavailable.
The table's concentration denominator is not explicitly labeled as DM even though the analytical method used dried plant material.
No regulatory thresholds, source comparison values or Dutch transfer factors are included in this measurement dataset.
Reference-only. No model parameter, default, equation or calculation is activated.
conversion_or_processing: Values transcribed without unit conversion, imputation, censoring substitution, or transfer to Dutch conditions.
uncertainty: Table 3 reports weighted means without standard deviations or confidence intervals. Censoring limits are preserved separately.
